characters.name: Billy Sparks
characters.description: The Cooper family's neighbor, who's the same age as Sheldon and Missy. Abhorrent Admirer: He has a one-sided crush on Missy. Adaptational Nice Guy: Sheldon describes him as a bully inThe Big Bang Theorybut inYoung Sheldon, he's on friendly terms with Sheldon and it's actually Billy's sister Bobbi who bullies Sheldon. The Bully: To Sheldon, but only in the pilot. After that, his little sister Bobbi takes on the bully role. Characterization Marches On: In his first appearance he is indeed shown bullying Sheldon, calling Sheldon a doofus and taunting him with his pet chicken Matilda. After that, Billy quickly becomes more of an emergency playmate/underling figure to Sheldon.

characters.name: Pastor Jeff Difford
characters.description: The pastor at the church Sheldon and his family attend. Also gives Sunday school to Sheldon, his sister, Billy Sparks and other kids. Ascended Extra: As of the Season 3 premiere "Quirky Eggheads and Texas Snow Globes", he is billed as part of the main cast. Awful Wedded Life: Proved to some extent by Selena not knowing Jeff's actual finances and he having to mistranslate what she says to the Cooper family. The plot of season 2's "A Broken Heart and a Crock Monster" is aboutPastor Jeff moving in with the Coopers after he and Selena stopped speaking to each other and hestarts sleeping on his office's couch. By the end of the episode,she dumps him because he is "un perdedor" (Spanish for "a loser"). Control Freak: In Season 6, he tries to force Meemaw to remove anything that doesn't fit his narrow Christian values from her video store. He even offers to come in and remove it all for her. Jeff only backs down when Meemaw threatens to openly reveal what R rated movies his wife and members of the church congregation rent from the video store. Fourth-Date Marriage:He and Robin get married rather abruptly because they want to become physically intimate, but Jeff can't do so outside of holy matrimony. It's not specified exactly how long they were together before tying the knot, but based on the episode airings, it can't have been longer than a few months.

characters.name: Ruben Alvarez
characters.description: Jim's employee at the tire store, and later the co-owner with Georgie. Family Relationship Switcheroo: His mom gave birth to him at 16, and then pretended to be his older sister for years. Jerk Jock: He regularly plays basketball. He's also incredibly nosy regarding Jim and Georgie's personal lives. Mistaken Nationality: He's Puerto Rican, but Georgie assumes he's Mexican.noteTo be fair to Georgie, Mexicans are one of the largest ethnic groups in Texas while the stateside Puerto Rican population is primarily concentrated around the Northeast and Florida. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: He admits to hating Georgie due to what he perceives as Jim playing favorites with his son-in-law over himself.

characters.name: Ms. VictoriaMacElroy
characters.description: Sheldon's homeroom teacher and English teacher at Medford High School. Although she previously looked out for Sheldon on his first day and was nice towards him, as soon as she learned of his rude attitude she disliked him. Apathetic Teacher: She clearly doesn't give a damn about her job, like the rest of Sheldon's teachers. Big Eater: She stress eats out of depression over gender inequality, claiming this as the reason why she's not the school principal. Though she's not overweight (yet). Formerly Fit: Sheldon's narrations indicate that she will become obese in the future as a result of her eating habits. Hypocrite: She complains that she wants to live long enough to see women no longer treated like second-class citizens while munching on a chili cheeseburger, high in trans fats and calories.

characters.name: Principal Tom Petersen
characters.description: The principal of Medford High School. Bearer of Bad News: He and Wayne inform the Cooper family thatGeorge has died. Benevolent Boss:When George and Mary found out that they were going to have another child, George asked Tom for a raise and Tom happily gave it to him. And even whenMary miscarried the childand George told Tom he didn't need the raise anymore, Tom still gave it to him. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He can be crude at times, but he does try his best to help Sheldon fit in at Medford High and treats George very well. He also comforts a distressed pregnant teen and tries to help Billy cope with his father leaving. Jerkass Has a Point: He pointed out to Ms.McElroy, Mr. Givens and Ms. Ingram that instead of relying on Sheldon to raise the school's test curve, they could simply do a better job at teaching the other students.

characters.name: Mr. Hubert Givens
characters.description: Sheldon's Science teacher at Medford High School. Out of all the teachers in the school, he seems to hate Sheldon the most. Apathetic Teacher: He clearly doesn't give a damn about his job, like the rest of Sheldon's teachers. Hidden Depths: Despite all of his apathy and bad attitude as a teacher, Mr. Givens is revealed to be a bigLost in Spacefan and attends the same comic convention as Sheldon in one episode. He's also familiar withStar Trek: The Original Seriesand gets into a passionate argument with Sheldon about which show is better. I Need a Freaking Drink: He is shown drinking with George and Wayne in the season three finale. Seeing Sheldon there (long story) likely didn't do him any favors. Jerkass: Unlike the rest of Sheldon's teachers, who seem to respect Sheldon deep down, he appears to have nothing but utter disdain for Sheldon and makes no attempts to hide it. While the rest of Sheldon's teachers genuinely praise his talents, Mr. Given's testimony in Sheldon's college video is basically just begging Mary to let Sheldon go to college, offering to help out in any way he can, including packing up his stuff for him. That said, time away from Sheldon appears to have softened his stance and when he comes to visit during Season 7, Mr. Givens seemssincerely thrilled at hearing Sheldon has been accepted into Caltech, even earnestly wishing him good luck (or that a random universe works out in his favor since Sheldon doesn't believe in luck).

characters.name: Ms. Evelyn Ingram
characters.description: Sheldon's Math teacher at Medford High School. Like most of the teachers at school, she seems to hate Sheldon. Apathetic Teacher: She clearly doesn't give a damn about her job, like the rest of Sheldon's teachers. Though it's revealed in the season 3 finale that Sheldon actually inspired her to take her job more seriously by studying every night just to keep up with him. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: She isn't very nice to Sheldon or any of her other students, but she does speak well of him in the video he made to convince Mary to go to college. And unlike the last time Sheldon tried to get into college, it seems like this time it was legit, and not just because she wants him gone. She even admits that she spent every night studying material in order to keep up with Sheldon. Sassy Black Woman: Normally averted, but she does turn up the sass when Sheldon gets on her nerves, which anyone else would do in that situation.

characters.name: Coach Wayne Wilkins
characters.description: Sheldon's P.E. teacher and assistant football coach at Medford High. Bearer of Bad News: He and Tom inform the Cooper family thatGeorge has died. Happily Married: George is somewhat jealous over how much better Wayne's marriage seems to be than his own. Until he realizes that Wayne and his wife don't have any children. Subverted by "An Ugly Car, an Affair and Some Kickass Football", where it's revealed thatDarlene has been cheating on Wayne. Hypocrite: He tends to give others health advice despite not being in very good shape himself.One example comes from "An Eagle Feather, a String Bean and an Eskimo", where Sheldon points out how hypocritical is of him to ask his students to run twenty laps when he is not willing to lead by example.In "A Proposal and a Popsicle Stick Cross", he encourages George not to eat a donut for health reasons. One example comes from "An Eagle Feather, a String Bean and an Eskimo", where Sheldon points out how hypocritical is of him to ask his students to run twenty laps when he is not willing to lead by example.

characters.name: Ms. Sheryl Hutchins
characters.description: The Medford High School librarian and pretty much the only staff member at the the school who can tolerate Sheldon due to her being a depressed loner. She is often complaining about how lonely she is, though later begins dating someone, but it has to be a secret as it is Mr. Givens, a Co-Worker. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: She's a great librarian and quite helpful to Sheldon despite her personal issues. Butt-Monkey: She's perpetually single, friendless, has cats who often run away and was accidentally tackled and seriously injured during a football game. Crazy Cat Lady: She tries to be this, but her cats have a habit of running away. The Eeyore: To say that she's a depressed, insecure sad sack would be a massive understatement.

characters.name: Tam Nguyen
characters.description: A Vietnamese teenage boy who was also the childhood friend and classmate of Sheldon Cooper. Tam is Sheldon's only friend in high school. Asian and Nerdy: He's the one who introduces Sheldon to comic books and role-playing games for the first time. Broken Bird: Somewhat sullen and pessimistic because of hisDark and Troubled Past. He appears to have PTSD. The Bus Came Back: He disappeared after season 4 but returned in season 7 episode "A New Home and a Traditional Texas Torture". Casanova Wannabe: Look at one of the reasons his and Sheldon's friendship with Libby broke up:because Tam tried to hit on her when they went without Sheldon to that IMAX movie and she didn't like it.

characters.name: Libby
characters.description: An aspiring geologist who briefly befriends Sheldon and Tam. Black and Nerdy: A black girl who's interested in geology. Innocently Insensitive: She referred to spending time with Sheldon as "babysitting", which hurt Sheldon very deeply to the point where he swore eternal hatred against geology over it. She certainly wasn't intending to be mean-spirited. One-Shot Character: She only appears in Season one episode "Dolomite, Apple Slices, and a Mystery Woman". Small Role, Big Impact: She's only in one episode, but is the main catalyst to Sheldon's contempt against geology which he'd carry with him to adulthood.

characters.name: Ira Rosenbloom
characters.description: One of Connie's suitors. He owns the local furniture store and he's Jewish. Dogged Nice Guy: Right after Connie decides in favor of John, he starts showering her with expensive gifts — often from his store — to the point of annoying her. He stops this after getting better acquainted with John. Friendly Rivalry: With Dr. Sturgis. They become friends when they fight for Connie's attention and remain so after she prefers John — especially after they got to meet each other at Ira's furniture store. In fact, when John broke up with Connie, he told her he'd like for her to get back with Ira. Love Triangle: Connie, Ira and Dr. Sturgis. He tries one with Coach Dale in place of the Dr., but it doesn't go anywhere besides a date and him crashing her date with the Coach. Nice Guy: He's very amiable and doesn't take a grudge on Connie preferring Dr. Sturgis (except for what's mentioned inDogged Nice Guy).

characters.name: Herschel Sparks
characters.description: The Coopers' next door neighbor, husband of Brenda Sparks and father of Billy and Bobbi Sparks. He works as a mechanic and recognized Georgie's knack for auto repairs, hiring him part-time after school. Foil: To George Cooper. Both of them are overweight members of the same neighborhood with a very peculiar son (George has Sheldon, a mouthyChild Prodigy, Herschel has Billy, who has some sort of mild developmental delays) and wives who boss them around. While George's marriage to Mary gets close to ending but they make up and remain married, Herschel's reaches the breaking point, and he divorces Brenda and moves away. Grease Monkey: Works as a mechanic and puts Georgie on the path to becoming Dr. Tire. Henpecked Husband: Constantly yelled at and bossed around by Brenda. He and George both bond over how they are often dominated by their wives. Nice Guy: Unlike his wife, he's always courteous to the Coopers.

characters.name: Selena
characters.description: Pastor Jeff's ex-wife who doesn't speak a word of English and has nothing in common with Pastor Jeff. Beauty Is Bad: She's very beautiful, but also rude, selfish and implied to be abusive towards Jeff. Credit Card Plot: She used Jeff's credit card to purchase a $2,000 massage chair. Domestic Abuser: Implied. Jeff asks Mary to accompany him when he returns home, in case Selena decides to come at him with a knife. Foil: To Robin. While both are known to have been married to Pastor Jeff, Selena is Hispanic, not very nice, a gold digger and doesn’t really like Pastor Jeff while Robin is American, a kind woman, doesn’t steal money and loves and cares for Pastor Jeff deeply.

characters.name: Peg
characters.description: Pastor Jeff's chain-smoking secretary. Dirty Old Woman: She displays many un-Christian behaviors in church, such as her smoking and drinking habits. In S5 E6, she is perfectly okay talking about sex at church, while Pastors Jeff and Rob are not. Smoky Voice: Peg's voice is very rough and gravelly due to her smoking habit. Stopped Caring: Her boyfriend served in World War II, and came home with syphilis. Since then, she has not dated anyone.

characters.name: Mr. Gene Lundy
characters.description: The drama teacher at Medford High School. Also dabbles in real estate on the side. Bad "Bad Acting": He can be a good actor when he wants to be, but his feigned sadness towards Sheldon for saying he can't help Mr. Lundy sell the house next door is so horrible that anyone other than Sheldon would be able to see right through it. Cross-Cast Role: In-universe, he plays the role ofAnniein the school play, when Sheldon drops out of the role at the last moment. Jerkass Has a Point: While he does take over Mary's Hell House project in "Seven Deadly Sins and a Small Carl Sagan", many of the liberties he has taken are actually valid: sin is supposed to be appealing, or else no one would be tempted to commit it. Large Ham: As expected of an unsuccessful theatre actor, even when he's not acting. He hams it up big time when portraying Satan in the Hell House.

characters.name: Bobbi Sparks
characters.description: Billy’s younger sister, who has a reputation of tormenting Sheldon. The Bully: To Sheldon. Despite her young age and smaller stature, Bobbi gets a penchant for tormenting Sheldon whenever he passes by her house, and takes advantage of being a cute little girl to get away with it. Decomposite Character: In TBBT, Sheldon describes her brother Billy as his childhood bully, but in YS, it's Bobbi who shows to regularly pick on Sheldon, while Billy doesn't seem to have a mean bone in his body. The Fake Cutie: Sheldon's family is shocked that such a seemingly innocent girl could be a bully. Meemaw says that's probably why she can get away with it. One-Shot Character: She only appears in the Season one episode "Jiu-Jitsu, Bubble Wrap, and Yoo-hoo".

characters.name: Brenda Sparks
characters.description: The wife of Herschel Sparks and the mother of Billy and Bobbi Sparks. She works at the bowling alley that Connie goes to. The Alcoholic: It is mentioned that she drinks a lot. In "An Academic Crime and a More Romantic Taco Bell", she organizes a meeting between all the baseball mothers, but it's really just an excuse to get drunk. Best Friend: Despite the rough start, she's more or less become this to Mary in the later seasons of the show. Big Beautiful Woman: She's heavyset, but fairly attractive, and implied to get attention from both Georgethough they never anything with each otherand Mr. Givens. Break the Haughty: Her bitchy attitude is taken down a few pegs after Herschel leaves her. Bonding with Mary over their respective issues also helps.

characters.name: Dr. John Sturgis
characters.description: A physics professor at East Texas Tech, the university Sheldon is auditing coursework for, and is dating Meemaw. Specifically, Sheldon is learning quantum chromodynamics in Sturgis's class. Amicable Exes: To a fair extent, he and Connie are this as they are still friends well into Season 4... this does getPlayed Within Season 5 when John finds out Dale and Connie broke up and plans to make a move on Connie again. Celebrity Paradox: Wallace Shawn appears as Dr. John Sturgis. Shawn's most famous roles are inThe Princess BrideandToy Story, both of which have been mentioned many times onThe Big Bang Theory. In fact, onToy Story, he appeared on the first two movies with Annie Potts (Meemaw onYoung Sheldon) and on the first three withLaurie Metcalf(Mom onTheory). Commuting on a Bus: In season 4, as he moved to Waxahachie to work on a supercollider. He occasionally gets phone calls from Sheldon and Connie. He returns to Medford in the penultimate episode of season 4. Doomed by Canon: Seeing as how he doesn't appear nor is referenced inThe Big Bang Theory, his romance with Connie is this. It's likely that either he'll die at some point or they will eventually break up.It seems to be the latter though as John broke up with her in the Season 3 episode "A Pineapple and the Bosom of Male Friendship".

characters.name: Paige Swanson
characters.description: AChild Prodigywho takes Dr. Sturgis' class alongside Sheldon. She's not only smarter than Sheldon, but also more social as well. Sheldon views her as a rival, but Paige is always kind towards him. Always Someone Better: And this is why Sheldon views her as a nuisance. She not only comes off as more intellectually gifted (for one, she's fluent in three languages while Sheldon only knows English and some Spanish, along with conversational Klingon), but has better social skills as well. And she is a month younger, making her both the youngest and smartest person in Dr. Sturgis' class. In the long run it's subverted, as she becomes aTragic Dropoutin college and turns to substance abuse, as opposed to Sheldon graduating and slowly ( okay,veryslowly) coming into his own socially inThe Big Bang Theory. Berserk Button: Poking fun at her parents' divorce, especially if you insinuate that it's her fault. Sheldon did this and earned a black eye for his trouble. Broken Ace: She may be a Child prodigy, but between her parents' divorce and the discrimination she faced at college, she became so miserable that she dropped out of college and turned to substance abuse. Distaff Counterpart: To Sheldon, being a femaleChild Prodigywho knows more than the adults.

characters.name: Linda Swanson
characters.description: Education Mama: She constantly pushes Paige to excel in school, even when Paige doesn't want to.

characters.name: Veronica Duncan
characters.description: A troubled teen who becomes a Born-again Christian. She is the object of Georgie's affection. Beware the Nice Ones: Being a born-again Christian didn't stop her from giving Georgie a black eye in retaliation for kissing her without permission during their baptism. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She hasn't appeared nor been mentioned since season 3 episode "An Academic Crime and a More Romantic Taco Bell". This is likely due to Isabel May working on other projects. She was finally mentioned in the series finale. Dark and Troubled Past: She was abandoned by her father and her older sister is in prison for trying to sell drugs to a cop. Disappeared Dad: As mentioned above, her father left when she was very young and her mother's boyfriend is a drunkenJerkass.

characters.name: Dr. Grant Linkletter
characters.description: A professor and colleague of Dr. Sturgis. He constantly tries to woo Connie away from him, to no avail. Sheldon audits his course during John's recovery and he becomes Sheldon's mentor once the latter starts attending full time. Child Hater: Part of the reason he wants to be free of Sheldon is because he doesn't understand him and dislikes being around children. Everyone Has Standards: He may not be very fond of Dr. Sturgis, but he seems to take his side when Sheldon accuses John of plagiarism. He informs Sheldon that scientists frequently exchange ideas, warns him that this accusation could have severe consequences and insists on talking to John himself before Sheldon takes the issue to the higher-ups. Hopeless Suitor: He regularly pursues Connie, even when she's with John, (and he knows that). This happens later when she is with Dale. He fails miserably every time. Even when she finally agrees to go out with him in "Future Worf and the Margarita of the South Pacific", it's clear that she only did it because he wore her down and she had nothing better to do. Not to mention she's clearly bored and uncomfortable on the date itself. Jerkass: If coming on to another man's girlfriend in front of said man isn't enough to qualify him as this, he also regularly uses Sheldon to get closer to Connie, allowing Sheldon to take his class while John is recovering at the mental hospital, asking Connie to an event in front of Sheldon so that she can't say no, lying when Sheldon asks Linkletter if he is using Sheldon to get closer to his Meemaw. Not to mention he doesn't really like Sheldon (at least outside their science experiments), even taking into account the latter's abrasiveness, only opportunistically doing so to be closer to Connie. All and all, he's a real piece of shit.

characters.name: Robin Difford
characters.description: A policewoman in Medford, and Pastor Jeff's wife. The Bus Came Back: In the Season 7 premiere "Half A Wiener Schnitzel And Underwear In A Tree" for the first time since the Season 3 episode "A House for Sale and Serious Woman Stuff" (S 3 E 19), a span of 65 episodes. Fair Cop: She's a very beautiful police officer. Foil: To Selena. While both are known to have been married to Pastor Jeff, Selena is Hispanic, not very nice, a gold digger and doesn't really like Pastor Jeff while Robin is American, a kind woman, doesn’t steal money and loves and cares for Pastor Jeff deeply. Fourth-Date Marriage:She and Pastor Jeff get married rather abruptly because they want to become physically intimate, but Jeff can't do so outside of holy matrimony. It's not specified exactly how long they were together before tying the knot, but based on the episode airings, it can't have been longer than a few months.

characters.name: Marcus Larson
characters.description: A baseball player and Missy's boyfriend during Seasons 3 and 4. Graceful Loser: When Missy's team has a game against his, she's afraid he'll lose interest in her if she scores the point that loses him the game. He doesn't, as when their teams are high-fiving each other in sportmanship after hers wins thanks to her, he holds her hand and wraps his fingers around hers, confirming that he still wants to go out with her. Satellite Love Interest: Has only had one linenote"Good game."during the series (as of the season 4 finale). Small Role, Big Impact:Missy's breakup with Marcus in the Season 4 finale causes the entire family to get into an argument, setting the stage for George possibly having an affair and the family breaking up.The Season 5 premiere strongly supports this theory.

characters.name: Coach Dale Ballard
characters.description: Missy's baseball coach and Connie's boyfriend. He also owns a sporting goods store and hires Georgie, and later George Sr., as a salesman. Casting Gag: He's portrayed byCraig T. Nelson, who's famous for previously portraying another fictionalcoach. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: Dale isn't the brightest bulb, and most of his attempts to play the tough guy just lead to him coming across as ineffectual, for which he's regularly mocked by Connie. However, when dealing with a guy attempting to extort him and Connie over them purchasing slot machines from him, after realising where this is going, Dale casually knocks the much younger man out cold with a single punch to the face. He evenapologised beforehand as he would rather it not come to this. Derailing Love Interests: While it may be too soon to say, the way he treats Dr. Sturgis in the latter portion of season 3 seems to signal that he's headed in this direction. Though to be fair, he has shown some jerkass qualities ever since he was first introduced and John is not entirely undeserving.He finally crosses fully into this in "A Baby Tooth and The Egyptian God of Knowledge" when Connie rejects his offer to get married. Not only does he take on anEntitled to Have Youattitude, but he fires Georgie the next day. While Georgie did leave the cash register open while he was in charge of the store, leading to over $400 being stolen, it's obvious that Dale only fired Georgie because he was pissed at Connie.He and Connie split up for real when Connie says she's not ready to slow and settle down with him.Zigzagged in that they eventually rekindle their relationship and are still together as ofGeorgie and Mandy's First Marriage, though it's still unclear how much longer it'll last. He and Connie split up for real when Connie says she's not ready to slow and settle down with him.

characters.name: Jana Boggs
characters.description: A cheerleader who Georgie dates. Alpha Bitch: Jana is a popular, talented cheerleader dating Georgie, a Football player. Amicable Exes: Downplayed. She's upset after Georgie breaks up with her but seems to smile a bit when he offers to drive her home so she doesn't have to walk. Though they get back together in season 4. Brainy Brunette: Possibly. While Jana doesn’t appear to be very academic, and couldn’t tell what Sheldon was saying in Spanish to her, it’s possible that she might be more clever than people think, as she was much more knowledgeable about early pregnancy factors and Science than Georgie, even if this wasn’t a very difficult thing to accomplish. Clingy Jealous Girl: She makes it very clear that she doesn't want Georgie to so much as look at other girls besides her. She also doesn't react well to Georgie still hanging out with Veronica, perhaps for good reason, since it's painfully evident that the two have feelings for each other.

characters.name: June
characters.description: Dale's ex-wife, who is the local hairdresser. Chatty Hairdresser: Apparently, as shown by the first time Mary went there, her clients actually go there more to talk to her than for hairdressing services,to the pointshe actually wonders whether she should start charging by the hour. Hollywood Tone-Deaf: When she and Connie go to a casino together, she demonstrates her terrible singing voice. This is likely aCasting Gagdue to her actress being a very famous singer. May–December Romance: In one episode, she appears for a double date with Connie and Dale with a much younger boyfriend. Dale even refers to the guy as a "toyboy". It doesn't seem to last though. Odd Friendship: She gets along very well with Connie, her ex-husband's new girlfriend.

characters.name: Sam
characters.description: One of Sheldon's fellow physics students. The Cassandra: In an attempt to ease the tensions between them, Sam tries to advise Sheldon that his haughty attitude is keeping him from having friends. He prefers to think that people avoid him out of deference to his intelligence and ignores her for the time being. Green-Eyed Monster: She is clearly jealous that Sheldon's dorm room is a single with its own bathroom, while she has to share a bedroom with two other people and a bathroom with 30. Odd Friendship: Sam has a distant if not hostile relationship with Sheldon due to his arrogance and privileges, but gets along great with his mother when they tour the campus together.

characters.name: Prof. Dora Ericson
characters.description: A philosophy professor. The Anti-Nihilist: After Sheldon has an existential crisis due to her class, she consoles him with her worldview of epistemology giving life meaning instead of making life seem pointless. Barefoot Loon: She kicks off her shoes in the class and encourages her students to do likewise, to demonstrate her free-spiritedness. Characterizing Sitting Pose: She teaches while sitting cross-legged on her desk, which demonstrates her nonconformism. Hippie Teacher: She has a laid-back teaching style, is very passionate about philosophy (especially her then-trendy post-modern ideas), and even invites her students to take off her shoes — which, according to Sheldon, some do (although, not Sheldon himself).

characters.name: President Linda Hagemeyer
characters.description: The president of East Texas Tech. Head-in-the-Sand Management: Thinks its a good idea to lie to Sheldon about the Grand Chancellor thinking it won't bite her in the ass, she's wrong. Hidden Depths: The episode where Sheldon tried staying at her house indicates she and her husband aren't religious, but they say Sheldon was free to do praying if she wanted, implying that she's respectful towards people of faith. Mistaken for Servant: In "A Free Scratcher and Feminine Wiles", she explains to Dr. Lee that during her first month as president, everyone thought she was the president's secretary. In response to this, she told them that the president was too busy to see them, and then cut their funding. Yes-Man: Zigzagged. She gives Sheldon a second phone line so that he can use the modem without being interrupted, and later gives him a dorm room (that's nicer than most of the rooms on campus) just for downtime in between classes. However, she also casually lies to Sheldon about her (non-existent) boss, the "Grand Chancellor", and feels no remorse for it.

characters.name: Gary O'Brien
characters.description: A rich benefactor of East Texas Tech, and a promoter of pseudoscience and conspiracy theories. Conspiracy Theorist: He perpetrates several of these, including that NASA faked the Apollo moon landings.

characters.name: Pastor Rob
characters.description: A youth pastor hired by Pastor Jeff to teach Sunday school. Good Shepherd: Unlike Pastor Jeff, he discourages theReligion Is Rightapproach. Instead, he encourages the children not to get too caught up in the text of the Bible and instead think for themselves to develop their relationship with God. Even Sheldon can't help but respect him. Sexy Priest: Both Mary and Missy are secretly attracted to him and fantasize about him. What Happened to the Mouse?: He disappears from the show after the season 6 episodeA Launch Party and a Whole Human Being. But it's likely he moved to Arkansas for the new pastor job after receiving a job offer there. Younger and Hipper: His approach to preaching religion screams this, compared to Pastor Jeff and Mary. He even encourages the children to think for themselves about religion, evenSheldonisimpressedby this approach.

characters.name: Jake Rutledge
characters.description: A Medford police officer. He's a friend of Dale's but an antagonist of Connie because ofhis shake down of her. Actor Allusion: He's played by Bill Fagerbakke and introduced as an old friend of Dale, played by Craig T Nelson, who are both best known for their roles onSeries/Coach Dirty Cop: First he shuts down Connie'sgambling den not because he thinks it's wrong but because he wants to use it as a campaign strategy because he's running for sheriff. Then when Connie findsa loophole, he shakes her down saying it's a gray area, and threatens her with jailtime, unless she paid him off.

characters.name: Prof. Boucher
characters.description: An engineering professor and Army Corps of Engineers veteran. Freudian Excuse: Combined withSmall Role, Big Impact, though not for this series butBig Bang. Boucher isa very strict, no-nonsense professor that constantly rejected and tore up Sheldon's work for being wrong. Unlike other professors, he adamantly refused to help Sheldon develop an understanding of his class's subject by telling him what he was doing wrong. It culminates in him closing the door in Sheldon's face when he was late to class, right after Sheldon finally figured out what was wrong with his work (the wind). Overall, this one man became the whole foundation for why Sheldon hates and looks down upon Engineering itself. Not So Above It All: Despite beingas strict as he is to Sheldon, he doesfind amusement in winning a disagreement with the President of the University, and willingly recreates Sheldon's shocked face from when he closed the door in his face to amuse Hagemeyer. Schedule Fanatic: He espouses military time in casual conversation, locks the classroom door at the start of class as a deterrent to late students, and points out to Sheldon about how his "fun fact" caused the class to fall one minute behind schedule. Sheldon eventually ends up a victim himself of Boucher's strictness and it colors his opinion of engineers well into his adult years.

characters.name: Oscar & Darren
characters.description: Sheldon's dorm neighbors at East Texas Tech. They and Sheldon frequently play video and tabletop games together. Early-Bird Cameo: Darren appears in "A Pager, a Club and a Cranky Bag of Wrinkles" as a student who studies by himself in Sheldon's Professor Proton Appreciation Club meeting (which no one else showed up to). Just Friends: Abby apparently made it very clear that she only likes Darren as a friend. Manchild: Lampshaded in S5 E17.Darren:We're basically 12.

characters.name: Abby
characters.description: Oscar & Darren's friend who playsDungeons & Dragonswith them. Nerd Nanny: Lampshaded in S5 E13.Darren:You're the closest to a mommy here. Vomit Chain Reaction: In S5 E13.Abby:If [Sheldon] throws up, I throw up!

characters.name: Dr. Carol Lee
characters.description: A physicist from UC Berkeley brought in to lead a project that Sheldon, Dr. Sturgis, and Dr. Linkletter are working on. Asian and Nerdy: An Asian-American physicist, played by Chinese-American actress Ming-Na Wen. Nerd Nanny: President Hagemeyer brings her in to lead the telescope project because, along with her scientific credentials, as a mother of three, she knows how to deal with the immature Sturgis, Linkletter and Sheldon. Territorial Smurfette:Dr. Lee:Can you believe there were only three women in my major?President Hagemeyer:Well, at least you had each other.Dr. Lee:Those bitches? Pass.

characters.name: Roy
characters.description: A football booster at the high school that has problems with how George is running the football team. Jerkass: Anytime he's onscreen, he's constantly grilling George over his leadership as the football team's captain. Jerkass Has a Point: He's needlessly mean about it, but Roy isn't entirely wrong to criticize some of the decisions George makes during a football game. Kick the Dog: Reveals to George that he's going to lose his job when he rejects his attempt at goodwill. Pet the Dog: He tries being chummy with George when running into him at the bar and offers to buy him a drink. However, George rejects this,leading to Roy's aforementioned KickTheDog moment.

characters.name: Amber
characters.description: Georgie's girlfriend for a few episodes. Romantic False Lead: She flirts with Georgie at the video store, and Mandy's okay with it and encourages Georgie to start dating her. Later, both Georgie and Mandy regret their decisions, and get back together as anOfficial Couple.

characters.name: Prof. Salzman
characters.description: A German physics professor who teaches Sheldon during his summer abroad. Stern Teacher: Calls Sheldon a "dummkopf" in front of the whole class.

characters.name: Mei-Tung Chen
characters.description: Sheldon's classmate from Germany, who's the same age as him. She tutors him after he struggles in the class. Asian and Nerdy: An AsianChild Prodigy. Distaff Counterpart: To Sheldon, as both of them as areChild Prodigies. Stern Teacher: She whacks his knuckles whenever he gives a wrong answer.

characters.name: Evan
characters.description: Sheldon's roommate at East Texas Tech. Only in It for the Money: Evan is convinced that computer science will make him rich. By contrast, Sheldon just wants to do science for its own sake.

characters.name: Nick
characters.description: Mandy's ex-boyfriend. The Alcoholic: He drinks heavily, and talks about being sober while drinking beer. He claims that only hard liquor counts as drinking.

characters.name: Beth
characters.description: Mandy's co-worker at the diner. Mama Bear: Beth rightfully threatens to kick the crap out of Georgie if he ever threatens Todd again, and fights Mandy when she insinuates that it was Todd's fault. Slut-Shaming: Refers to her son's girlfriend as a slut who's leading Todd down the wrong path, unaware that said girlfriend is Mandy's sister-in-law Missy. When she doubles down on insulting Missy after learning her relation to Mandy, the latter gets into an argument with Beth that escalates into a fistfight.

characters.name: Todd
characters.description: Beth's son, who's only a year younger than Georgie. Also Missy's boyfriend in "Two Idiots on a Dirt Bike". Dumbass Teenage Son: He wants to ride his motorbike while drunk, despite Georgie's warnings. When he runs away with Missy to get married, he only brings his $10 allowance with him, prompting Missy to call off the marriage. Elopement: Tries to run away with Missy on an impulsive act, but it goes south, among other things, because he only brought his$10 allowance with him. One Degree of Separation: He turns out to be an ex-colleague of Georgie's, having attended the same school a year below him.

characters.name: Valerie
characters.description: A woman who Georgie tows; she then flirts with him to Mandy's chagrin. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Valerie is a churchgoing gorgeous woman, and after Georgie comes to help her with her car, she invites him to go visit her church in what Georgie insists is a completely innocuous friendship, but as soon as she gets a moment alone with him, she comes on him, insisting that their meeting was a sign from God and tries to seduce him, despite knowing he's married. Hypocrite: She's devoted to her church and often talks about how her faith gave her everything she has, but tries to seduce Georgie despite knowing that he's married and insisting that their meetings were only a friendship. Laser-Guided Karma: She lured Georgie under the pretense that she wanted to show him her church and be his friend, only to try to seduce him despite knowing he was married and happily so. Mandy, who had chosen to follow them that night, walks in on them as Valerie is coming on to Georgie and promptly knocks her lights out with a punch.

characters.name: Fred Fagenbacher
characters.description: The owner of a competing tire store, and Audrey's ex-boyfriend. Intergenerational Rivalry: With Georgie after the latter took over Jim's tire business. Fred went to school with Jim and Audrey, who are implied to be older than Georgie's parents. The Rival: To Jim in the tire business, and later to Georgie, when the latter buys Jim's store and becomes Fred's main competition. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: To Jim, as they're simultaneously economic and romantic competitors. Trophy Wife: Fred and his wife Diana run into Jim and Audrey, and Audrey asks whether Diana is Fred's daughter.

characters.name: Chloe Costa
characters.description: An employee at Connor's favorite music store, and later Connor's girlfriend. Friends with Benefits: She and Connor breal up after aPregnancy Scare, but rekindle and decide to keep being friends... who have sex. Obnoxious In-Laws: She runs away after meeting Audrey for the first time. Slap-Slap-Kiss: Her first kiss with Connor is after arguing with him over whetherSteely DanorThe Ramonesis better. Starving Artist: She was a touring musician in her previous boyfriend's band, but then he dumped and abandoned her in Medford.

characters.name: Scott
characters.description: Mandy's ex-boyfriend, and her new boss at Channel 7 as of "Guilt Boots". Parent-Preferred Suitor: Audrey isn't shy about mentioning that she thinks Scott would've made a much better husband for Mandy than Georgie, not least because he has rich parents. Working with the Ex: He's Mandy's boss and ex-boyfriend.

characters.name: Kelli
characters.description: Mandy's replacement at Channel 7. Friendly Rivalry: After making some escalating jabs at each other, she and Mandy decide to be civil but keep their feud in front of the cameras. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: To Mandy, naturally. They make up in "A Little Schmoozin' and a Nose for the News" but keep their feud going publicly for the ratings.

characters.name: Lindsey
characters.description: Mandy's new boss at Channel 9. Black Boss Lady: An African-American woman who runs Mandy's program in Channel 9. Everyone Has Standards: She doesn't mind Mandy using shady tactics to attract ratings and keeping her feud with Kelli, but asks Mandy if Kelli has anything really dirty to use against her to the point of ruining her reputation. Mandy, who got involved in some shady business with Connie, lies through her teeth that she doesn't. No Such Thing as Bad Publicity:In-Universe; she very much runs by this philosophy, hiring Mandy despite her controversial comments on God, and encouraging her to continue feuding with Kelli for ratings.

characters.name: Sheldon Cooper
characters.description: Abandoned Catchphrase: Sheldon adopted the habit of making some surprising statement, and when met with surprise, reveal that he was joking with the catchphrase "bazinga!" He also used it once when successfully pranking Leonard. He abandoned it after a while. Academia Elitism: Sheldon frequently mocks Howard for going to M.I.T. and Leonard for going Princeton. Accent Slip-Up: Jim Parsons manages to keep his natural Texan drawl under control but there are a few times it slips out, typically done in character with Sheldon whoinvokedis also from Texas. These relapses are rather cleverly worked into the story — it is heavily implied that Sheldon affects his rather colorless normal accent, and that his natural Texan accent creeps back into his speech when he is too angry, distressed or occasionally too drunk to hide it. For example, when Sheldon is locked out of his apartment and Penny offers to let him eat his food in her apartment:Penny:Sure, why not?Sheldon:[accent relapsing]Sure, why not? And after the sun sets, we can all go pile up in my pickup truck and go skinny-dipping down by the the crick! Cause today's the day to stop making sense! Accidental Hero: On multiple occasions. For instance, he stopped Leonard from giving up the secrets to the experimental rocket fuel to a spy posing as his date, by barging in and complaining about them trying to sleep together without warning him 24 hours in advance, as their roommate agreement required. He also has a lack of social filter, such as that he will attempt things that others are too timid to do themselves and by all means shouldn't work, but sometimes does. Especially when he nails anArmor-Piercing Questionon Leonard, it tends to prove beneficial to him in the long run by forcing him to confront that option. Actually Pretty Funny: When he laughs, he only does it for a second before resuming to his usual serious, stoic self but when Penny imitates Leonard, he actually could barely resist the urge to laugh at it. Fatal F
